transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. tell me your dream, however it comes back to you.
so the first part i remember is being at the meads’s house, but it was bigger inside than out.
that bigger inside than out thing, that's such a weird dream feeling. like the house had its own idea of space.
yeah exactly. just inside the front it was like a european village with a cobblestone street
a whole village just past the front door. were you walking that street, or just taking it in from where you stood?
kinda just taking it in at first, but there was this pied-piper sort of man with curly hair who could do things like juggle
a pied-piper man with curly hair. what was he doing when you first noticed him?
he was just there on the street, like showing off—juggling and stuff. didn't feel weird, just part of it
just part of the village, someone showing off on the cobblestones. did you stay and watch him, or did you move on?
i moved on pretty quick. went up some back stairs—the real house doesn't have any—then straight down the other side cos there was a second set right away
up one set and straight down another, like the house kept giving you ways through. did the second stairs look the same as the first?
i don't remember exactly how they looked, just that they were wooden and close together
wooden and close, yeah, that's all you need. where did you end up after going down the second set?
a short empty hallway that turns a corner. then i found a tiny room
tiny room. was it the kind of tiny that feels cozy, or the kind that makes you feel too big for it?
cozy, i think. there was a young woman with shoulder-length blonde hair in a pageboy in there, cooking at a stove that almost filled the room
a woman cooking at a stove that nearly fills the room. did you know her, or was she just someone there?
no, didn't know her. but she was nice to me. just felt okay in there
that's a good thing to land in—somewhere that feels okay. what happened after you'd been in there a while?
then i was outside, waiting for my aunt to pick me up
you went from that tiny cozy room to outside waiting. did the outside feel like the same place, or somewhere else entirely?
didn't say exactly, but it felt like a different spot. just standing out by the road
just standing out by the road, waiting. what was the wait like—did she take a long time to come?
no, she came pretty quick. arrived in a little round convertible
a little round convertible pulls up. did she say anything to you, or did you just hop in?
i don't remember saying much, just got in and went for a drive. not very far, we crossed a little bridge over a creek, then doubled back and she dropped me off at the house again
a short loop of a drive, over a creek and back. when she dropped you at the house, did it still feel like the same house from before?
i think it was the same, yeah. but it's a bit fuzzy. then i was inside—i think it was inside—sitting with a couple of people, playing with a string of blue balloons
blue balloons. did you feel grown in that moment, or more like a kid again?
more like a kid again, i think. just calm, playing with the balloons.
that calm with the balloons, it sounds like a soft place to be near the end of a dream. if you could pause the dream on one moment—the one that's stayed with you most—which moment would it be?
the tiny room with the woman at the stove. that's the one that keeps coming back to me
then let's stay there a minute. what did the light in that tiny room feel like—was it warm, dim, did it seem like day outside?
it felt warm, kind of soft. i don't know if it was day or night—can't remember that part
that's okay. warm and soft is enough. was there anything in that room besides the stove that felt important, like a particular object you noticed?
not that i remember. the stove was really the main thing, since it almost filled the room.

so you started at the meads's house, but inside it was bigger than outside. just past the door was a cobblestone village street with a curly-haired man juggling, like a pied piper. you didn't stay long, went up some narrow wooden back stairs and straight down another set into a short hallway and a tiny cozy room. a young woman with shoulder-length blonde hair in a pageboy was cooking at a stove that nearly filled the room, warm soft light, and it felt okay. then you were outside waiting for your aunt. she came quick in a little round convertible, you drove over a creek and back, and she dropped you at the house again. last you remember being inside with a couple of people, playing with blue balloons, feeling calm and more like a kid. the moment that stayed with you most is that tiny room with the woman at the stove.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah, you got it right. that's pretty much exactly it

i'll keep that dream with me. it's got such a soft, wandering feeling to it.

would you like to see it drawn?
yes, i'd like that

lovely, let's make it happen.

when you picture the dream, what kind of look feels truest to it? in your own words.
soft and warm, like a storybook but not too cartoonish. something gentle.

i have everything i need.

your dream will start appearing on the right as the pictures are ready.
